report.summary: Process metrics (code churn, prior faults) consistently predict bugs best, with AUCs 0.75–0.83 (D'Ambros 2010) and 0.76–0.81 (Kamei 2013). Complexity metrics (cyclomatic, LOC) achieve lower AUCs (≈0.6–0.7) and fail to generalize across projects. Dependency centrality shows mixed support; replication often reduces its effect. Process metrics hold up best on replication, while complexity metrics degrade.
risks: Cross-project prediction still drops AUC to ~0.5–0.6.
todos: Prioritize process metrics (churn, prior defects) in Daedalus defect predictor.
Validate JIT prediction model on own repository history.
Investigate if dependency centrality adds marginal benefit after process metrics.

handoff.suggestion: Build a just-in-time defect predictor using process metrics (e.g., number of distinct authors, recent change frequency, prior bug count) as primary signals. Reference work by Kamei et al. (2013) and D'Ambros et al. (2010) for feature engineering and validation approaches.
